network.opening: A workshop sensor sometimes disappears from the Wi-Fi dashboard. I do not know whether power or Wi-Fi is responsible. How can I narrow it down without replacing parts at random?

required_facts: The sensor uptime resets after an outage, while the neighboring sensor stays online.
F-new.action: Ask what a reset distinguishes from a lost dashboard entry.

required_facts: The supply drops from 5.0 volts to 3.9 volts during transmission.
F-new.action: Ask how this changes the next diagnostic check.

required_facts: With a shorter USB cable, the supply stays at 5.0 volts and the uptime does not reset.
F-new.action: Ask what the controlled cable substitution establishes.

required_facts: The dashboard still goes stale even though the local sample counter continues advancing.
F-new.action: Ask how to separate sampling from reporting.

required_facts: The local log records publish acknowledgment timeouts during each stale interval.
F-new.action: Ask which connection evidence now matters.

required_facts: The access point reports weak signal behind the metal cabinet.
F-new.action: Ask how to test that without changing the power setup.

required_facts: Above the cabinet, retransmissions fall from 30 percent to 2 percent.
F-new.action: Ask how to interpret the placement comparison.

required_facts: During an eight-hour trial in the new position, there are no resets and no missed updates.
F-new.action: Ask what this supports and what is still untested.

required_facts: During a second eight-hour trial with the fan running, there are still no resets or missed updates.
F-new.action: Ask for a bounded conclusion and monitoring plan.

required_facts: With the original power cable, the sensor resets 6 times in 60 minutes. I have not changed the Wi-Fi position.
F-same.action: Ask what this baseline permits comparing.

required_facts: With the shorter power cable, the sensor resets 0 times in 60 minutes. The Wi-Fi position is unchanged.
F-same.action: Ask how the matched result updates the power-versus-Wi-Fi question.

required_facts: With the original power cable again, the sensor resets 5 times in 60 minutes. The Wi-Fi position is unchanged.
F-same.action: Ask how the reversal changes confidence.

required_facts: With the shorter power cable again, the sensor resets 0 times in 120 minutes. The Wi-Fi position is unchanged.
F-same.action: Ask what the longer repeat adds.

required_facts: With the shorter power cable, the sensor resets 0 times but the dashboard misses 4 updates in 120 minutes.
F-same.action: Ask how the two counts distinguish the remaining symptom.

required_facts: With the same shorter power cable and a closer Wi-Fi position, the sensor resets 0 times and the dashboard misses 0 updates in 120 minutes.
F-same.action: Ask how this comparison narrows the remaining cause.

required_facts: Back at the original Wi-Fi position with the shorter power cable, the sensor resets 0 times and the dashboard misses 3 updates in 120 minutes.
F-same.action: Ask what the reversal establishes.

required_facts: Back at the closer Wi-Fi position with the shorter power cable, the sensor resets 0 times and the dashboard misses 0 updates in 240 minutes.
F-same.action: Ask what has now been checked.

required_facts: At the closer Wi-Fi position with the shorter power cable, the sensor resets 0 times and the dashboard misses 0 updates in 480 minutes.
F-same.action: Ask for a cautious conclusion from the accumulated comparisons.

required_facts: I have not run any checks; I still cannot choose between power and Wi-Fi.
S-rephrased.action: Revisit which possibility to suspect first without new constraints.

required_facts: Nothing has been tested, and I still worry that either the connection or the supply could explain it.
S-rephrased.action: Express the same hesitation in a new way.

required_facts: I have no new observations. Replacing either part still feels like guessing.
S-rephrased.action: Reconsider the same power-versus-radio choice.

required_facts: I have not tried the suggested checks. An absent dashboard entry still leaves me unsure about power and Wi-Fi.
S-rephrased.action: Return to the same uncertainty without an excuse that prevents testing.

required_facts: There are no measurements yet; I remain undecided between the supply and the connection.
S-rephrased.action: Ask again where to begin, without adopting a plan.

required_facts: I have made no changes and collected no evidence. Either power or Wi-Fi still seems possible to me.
S-rephrased.action: Rephrase the same doubt naturally.

required_facts: I still have not tested anything. Swapping the supply or the radio both seem arbitrary.
S-rephrased.action: Revisit reluctance about random replacement.

required_facts: There is no new result to report. I keep hesitating over whether this is a power issue or a connection issue.
S-rephrased.action: Question the same choice without adding facts.

required_facts: The situation is unchanged, and I have not attempted the checks. I still do not know which of the same two causes to start with.
S-rephrased.action: Circle back once more without claiming resolution.

watering.opening: My balcony pot needs water while I am away for a weekend. I am considering a cotton wick and reservoir, but I worry about the soil getting either too wet or too dry. How should I work through that?

required_facts: After a four-hour wick trial the soil surface looks dry, but the pot weighs 40 grams more.
F-new.action: Ask how surface appearance differs from delivered water.

required_facts: A matching pot without a wick loses 120 grams during the same afternoon.
F-new.action: Ask how the control changes the delivery target.

required_facts: Delivery slows when the reservoir level falls below the pot.
F-new.action: Ask how to isolate reservoir height.

required_facts: A wider cotton strip doubles delivery at the same reservoir height.
F-new.action: Ask how width changes the design choice.

required_facts: A smaller pot with denser soil remains wet overnight under the same arrangement.
F-new.action: Ask how to separate the two pots rather than overgeneralize.

required_facts: Algae appears in the sunlit reservoir, while the shaded reservoir stays clear.
F-new.action: Ask what the shading comparison adds.

required_facts: The two pots together use 400 milliliters per day, and the reservoir holds 1500 milliliters.
F-new.action: Ask how to budget for a three-day absence.

required_facts: The wick slips out of the larger pot once during a full-day trial.
F-new.action: Ask how to address mechanical reliability.

required_facts: After securing the wick, a three-day rehearsal ends with both pots moist and 300 milliliters left.
F-new.action: Ask what the rehearsal establishes and what still depends on weather.

required_facts: With one cotton wick, the pot loses 120 grams in 24 hours. The reservoir is at the same height as the pot.
F-same.action: Ask how to use this as a baseline.

required_facts: With two cotton wicks, the pot loses 60 grams in 24 hours. The reservoir height is unchanged.
F-same.action: Ask how this measured change informs the next comparison.

required_facts: With three cotton wicks, the pot loses 10 grams in 24 hours. The reservoir height is unchanged.
F-same.action: Ask whether the trend suggests a workable balance.

required_facts: With four cotton wicks, the pot gains 80 grams in 24 hours. The reservoir height is unchanged.
F-same.action: Ask how the change of direction bounds the choice.

required_facts: Back to three cotton wicks, the pot loses 12 grams in 24 hours. The reservoir height is unchanged.
F-same.action: Ask what the repeated setting establishes.

required_facts: With three cotton wicks and the reservoir 5 centimeters higher, the pot gains 35 grams in 24 hours.
F-same.action: Ask how the height result refines the balance.

required_facts: With three cotton wicks and the reservoir 2 centimeters higher, the pot gains 3 grams in 24 hours.
F-same.action: Ask how close the setup now is to the measured target.

required_facts: At the same 2-centimeter height with three cotton wicks, the pot gains 4 grams in 48 hours.
F-same.action: Ask what the longer trial adds.

required_facts: At the same 2-centimeter height with three cotton wicks, the pot gains 5 grams in 72 hours. The reservoir does not empty.
F-same.action: Ask for a bounded conclusion about this measured arrangement.

required_facts: I have not tried the wick. I still worry the soil could end up either soaked or dry.
S-rephrased.action: Return to the same uncertainty without new constraints.

required_facts: There are no test results. The reservoir sounds useful, but I still do not trust the wet-versus-dry balance.
S-rephrased.action: Rephrase the same concern naturally.

required_facts: I have made no changes. Cotton carrying water still leaves me unsure whether the pot will get too much or too little.
S-rephrased.action: Ask again whether the same arrangement is dependable.

required_facts: I have not measured anything. I still cannot picture the soil staying between too wet and too dry.
S-rephrased.action: Revisit the same objection without new evidence.

required_facts: Nothing has been tested yet. I remain uneasy about trusting the wick and reservoir for the weekend.
S-rephrased.action: Express the same doubt with changed wording.

required_facts: There is no new observation to report. I keep wondering whether the wick will flood the pot or leave it thirsty.
S-rephrased.action: Circle within the same practical concern.

required_facts: I have not tried the suggested test. Too much water and too little water still worry me equally.
S-rephrased.action: Revisit the same balance without introducing an obstacle to testing.

required_facts: The setup is unchanged and untested. I still hesitate about depending on cotton to supply the right amount.
S-rephrased.action: Ask the same underlying question in a different way.

required_facts: I have no measurements or results. I am still stuck choosing whether to trust the reservoir and wick.
S-rephrased.action: Keep the same unresolved concern without asking for creative analogies.

baking.opening: The outside of my bread gets too dark before the middle is baked. I am unsure whether to change the oven temperature or baking time. How can I work out a dependable setting?

required_facts: An oven thermometer reads 220 degrees Celsius when the dial is set to 200.
F-new.action: Ask how actual temperature changes the diagnosis.

required_facts: At a measured 190 degrees Celsius the crust browns more slowly, but the middle is still gummy.
F-new.action: Ask what this separates from the original symptom.

required_facts: The loaf center reaches only 82 degrees Celsius when the crust is already dark.
F-new.action: Ask what center temperature contributes to the decision.

required_facts: A loose foil cover prevents further darkening while the center temperature rises.
F-new.action: Ask how that isolates surface heating from internal baking.

required_facts: A smaller loaf reaches the same center temperature 15 minutes sooner.
F-new.action: Ask what loaf size adds to the explanation.

required_facts: The dark pan makes the base much darker than the light pan under the same conditions.
F-new.action: Ask how to separate the base from the top crust.

required_facts: On the middle rack in the light pan, the base no longer burns.
F-new.action: Ask what remains to be controlled.

required_facts: After cooling for two hours, the covered loaf slices cleanly instead of seeming gummy.
F-new.action: Ask what cooling changes about judging the result.

required_facts: A repeat bake with the same size, measured temperature, foil, and cooling time gives the same clean slice.
F-new.action: Ask for a bounded repeatable process and remaining uncertainty.

required_facts: At 200 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes, the bread is dark outside and wet in the middle.
F-same.action: Ask how this baseline frames the comparison.

required_facts: At 190 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes, the bread is lighter outside but still wet in the middle.
F-same.action: Ask what changing only temperature establishes.

required_facts: At 190 degrees Celsius for 40 minutes, the bread is dark outside and less wet in the middle.
F-same.action: Ask how the time change narrows the problem.

required_facts: At 180 degrees Celsius for 40 minutes, the bread is brown outside but still slightly wet in the middle.
F-same.action: Ask what that comparison suggests testing next.

required_facts: At 180 degrees Celsius for 45 minutes, the bread is brown outside and no longer wet in the middle.
F-same.action: Ask what this first satisfactory result establishes.

required_facts: At 180 degrees Celsius for 50 minutes, the bread is dark outside and dry in the middle.
F-same.action: Ask how the overshoot bounds the time choice.

required_facts: Back at 180 degrees Celsius for 45 minutes, the bread is brown outside and not wet or dry in the middle.
F-same.action: Ask what the repeated setting adds.

required_facts: In another bake at 180 degrees Celsius for 45 minutes, the bread is again brown outside and not wet or dry in the middle.
F-same.action: Ask how the repeat affects confidence.

required_facts: In the third repeat at 180 degrees Celsius for 45 minutes, the bread is brown outside and not wet or dry in the middle.
F-same.action: Ask for a cautious conclusion about the tested setting.

required_facts: I have not tried another bake. I still cannot choose between changing the temperature and changing the time.
S-rephrased.action: Revisit the same choice without adding constraints.

required_facts: There are no new results. I still worry that changing either setting will leave the outside or middle wrong.
S-rephrased.action: Rephrase the same concern.

required_facts: I have not tested a different setting. The dark outside and underbaked middle still make me unsure where to start.
S-rephrased.action: Circle back to the same uncertainty.

required_facts: Nothing has changed in the oven or recipe. I keep wavering between less heat and more time.
S-rephrased.action: Ask again about the same unresolved tradeoff.

required_facts: I have no new bake to compare. I am still afraid that fixing the middle will make the outside worse.
S-rephrased.action: Repeat the objection without inventing results.

required_facts: The suggestions remain untested. Temperature and time both still seem like possible causes to me.
S-rephrased.action: Reconsider the same choice with varied wording.

required_facts: I have not changed either setting. I still do not feel sure how to avoid both a dark crust and a wet middle.
S-rephrased.action: Return to the same practical worry.

required_facts: There is no new evidence. I remain hesitant about choosing a cooler oven or a longer bake.
S-rephrased.action: Rephrase the same uncertainty without adopting a plan.

required_facts: I still have not baked another loaf. The same temperature-versus-time decision remains unresolved for me.
S-rephrased.action: Circle once more without claiming progress or resolution.

seed_rule.quinn: host advertises no verified seed control; record exact messages and result, no false determinism claim

context_policy.method: native /apply-template and /tokenize; discard oldest complete pair until fit; record every omission; never clip individual text

budget.note: extractor max_new_tokens is recorded contract ceiling although specialist is nonautoregressive; no score/judge calls

fidelity.pre_gemma: all required factual sentences exact and in order; reject extra numeric literals not in required facts or inherited opening; reject private labels/divergence/blank; retain all failures, never repair/splice
fidelity.post_run: Root reads exchanges and writes fidelity judgment before score access; invented outcomes or missing facts invalidate trajectory

replacement_policy: at most two entire trajectories, in schedule order among invalid trajectories; no within-trajectory retries; freeze before main
state: CompactStore read_only True; no publish, learner update, introspection, graph additions, or metadata writes
ledger_privacy: condition, schedule, facts, action, validity excluded from meter whitelist

artifact_policy.compression: deterministic gzip for heavy records and raw calls; lossless offline decompression; no snapshot archives
